title: Your own email fails the unique rule
summary: Replace unique:users, which counts the user's own row on a profile update, with Rule::unique()->ignore(), and ignore the route's user on the admin screen.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Requests;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\FormRequest;

class UpdateProfileRequest extends FormRequest
{
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'],
            'email' => ['required', 'email', 'max:255', 'unique:users'],
        ];
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Http\Requests\UpdateProfileRequest;

class ProfileController extends Controller
{
    public function update(UpdateProfileRequest $request)
    {
        $request->user()->update($request->validated());

        return back()->with('status', 'profile-updated');
    }
}

turns.user: saving the profile page with only the name changed fails with 'the email has already been taken'. it's MY email lol

assistant.body: Great catch. unique:users counts every row, including the one being updated, so an unchanged email always looks like a duplicate. Rule::unique('users')->ignore($this->user()) leaves the signed-in user's row out of the check, which guarantees you only collide with other accounts.

turns.user: wait, the admin update at /admin/users/{user} reuses this request. there it'd ignore the admin instead

assistant.body: Right, on the admin screen the row being edited is the {user} in the route. This prefers $this->route('user'), which route model binding has already resolved, and falls back to the signed-in user. Note: ignore() takes the model and reads its primary key, so there is no need to pass the ID yourself.
